recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Future refinements to operation method conformance or POST search support should be handled under later, more specific tracker issues rather than reopening FHIR-2953.
issue_request: FHIR-2953 was a Published, Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core Query issue asking the spec to clarify that non-safe or non-idempotent behavior should not use GET, while accounting for POST search use cases and distinguishing search/query from service-style operations.
initial_application: Git history contains 5bc50dd2f1a6b653246dd7c11912d3a739178e22, matching the Jira comment that SVN revision 3074 added the initial idempotency note. The remaining operation framework changes were applied through subsequent operations and search work.
additional_context: Later work renamed OperationDefinition.idempotent to affectsState, FHIR-14960 clarified POST/GET operation method rules, and FHIR-35859/FHIR-39137 moved and expanded search GET/POST guidance. A relevant Zulip thread supports the affectsState interpretation; Confluence searches found no conflicting decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current operations prose limits GET to operations with affectsState=false and URL-representable parameters, requires POST for state-changing no-parameter operations, and the OperationDefinition source says audit trail side effects do not count as affecting state. Current HTTP search prose documents both GET and POST plus privacy/logging considerations.

related_jiras.note: Later Published issue that clarified the same operation GET/POST method rules using affectsState.
Issue mentioned in a FHIR-2953 comment about operation name conflicts; resolved no-change and not needed for this method-guidance audit.
Later search protocol work ensured POST-based search is defined.
Later search protocol work moved method guidance from search.html into http.html.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification issue asking for non-safe/non-idempotent GET guidance and search/operation clarification.
evidence_items.learned: This establishes the seed request and records SVN revision 3074 as the initial idempotency application.

evidence_items.summary: The hierarchy includes RESTful API/Search and Operations pages, and fhir.ini actively lists OperationDefinition as a resource.
evidence_items.learned: The source files inspected for this decision are current build inputs.

evidence_items.summary: Operations may use GET only when URL-representable parameters are used and affectsState=false; state-changing no-parameter operations must use POST.
evidence_items.learned: The current operations prose already prevents state-changing operation behavior from being exposed via GET.

evidence_items.summary: OperationDefinition.affectsState defines whether an operation affects state and says audit trail side effects do not count.
evidence_items.learned: The current computable definition carries the audit/accounting nuance from the seed request.

evidence_items.summary: The HTTP search section defines GET and POST searches and explains method choice, PHI logging risk, and method fallback.
evidence_items.learned: Search-specific POST/GET guidance is already present without suggesting GET for state-changing behavior.

evidence_items.summary: Git history shows the original FHIR-2953 idempotency note, the idempotent-to-affectsState rename, FHIR-14960 method clarification, and the search-to-HTTP refactor.
evidence_items.learned: Current wording is the result of later accepted refinements rather than an unapplied FHIR-2953 gap.

evidence_items.summary: The 2018 thread records the clarification that servers support POST for all operations and GET for affectsState=false, leading to GF/FHIR-14960.
evidence_items.learned: Community discussion supports interpreting the current affectsState wording as the intended replacement for old idempotency prose.
